title: Sundag
about: A piece for the open air, the mirror of Mondag (the caves). It is written for its biome as it stands, so every fader is 0 dB above ground. The game keeps playing it when the player goes underground, and it is meant to stand that; the 'cave' hint only thins the reed organ and the bell, the two lanes the cave reverb smears first. The roles say what each lane does.

roles.lead: the tune: the clarinet, and the horn's calls and its echo (bars 13–16), and the horn when it sings the tune (bars 25–28): keep it
roles.foundation: the picked guitar (its thumb marks every group of the 13/8 bar) and the plucked bass: the pulse and the floor: keep it
roles.bed: the reed organ holding two notes of each chord: already thin (nothing under 250 Hz); the first to smear under the cave reverb
roles.sparkle: a distant tubular bell, struck six times in the whole piece; it rings long

lanes.label: Horn
lanes.note: calls in bars 13–14, sings the tune in bars 25–28, holds the 7th harmonic in the last chord

lanes.label: Echo
lanes.note: the horn's call answered from across the valley (bars 15–16, 37), softer and panned the other way
